conventions.universe: All classes consist of total decision languages over {0,1}*. A language is a set of finite binary strings.
conventions.inclusion: A ⊆ B is set inclusion of language classes, never a reduction between classes.
conventions.separation: A ⊄ B means there exists a language in A outside B.
conventions.strict_inclusion: A ⊊ B abbreviates A ⊆ B and B ⊄ A; these are two different ordered-pair claims.
conventions.nonuniformity: AC0, ACC0, TC0, NC1, Ppoly and NPpoly allow arbitrary families/advice. They can contain undecidable languages. NC is logspace-uniform.
conventions.quantum: Quantum and interactive classes here contain total languages. Promise-problem variants are a separate possible track.
conventions.gates: Quantum gate-set precision and exact machine encodings must be fixed in the semantic Lean completion; these are mathematical class specifications, not completed operational formalizations.

classes.label: AC⁰
classes.definition: Nonuniform polynomial-size, constant-depth Boolean circuits with unbounded-fan-in AND/OR and NOT gates.

classes.label: ACC⁰
classes.definition: Nonuniform polynomial-size, constant-depth AC⁰ circuits also allowing MOD_m gates for one fixed integer m ≥ 2; union over fixed moduli.

classes.label: TC⁰
classes.definition: Nonuniform polynomial-size, constant-depth circuits with unbounded-fan-in majority and Boolean gates.

classes.label: NC¹
classes.definition: Nonuniform polynomial-size Boolean circuits with bounded fan-in and O(log n) depth.

classes.label: L
classes.definition: Languages decided by deterministic machines using O(log n) work space and a read-only input tape.

classes.label: NL
classes.definition: Languages decided by nondeterministic machines using O(log n) work space; acceptance means some computation accepts.

classes.label: LogCFL
classes.definition: Languages logspace many-one reducible to a context-free language.

classes.label: uniform NC
classes.definition: Languages decided by logspace-uniform, polynomial-size bounded-fan-in Boolean circuit families with depth O((log n)^k) for some fixed k.

classes.label: SC
classes.definition: Languages decided by one deterministic machine in polynomial time and O((log n)^k) work space simultaneously, for some fixed k.

classes.label: P
classes.definition: Union over k of DTIME(n^k), under standard finite-alphabet multitape Turing-machine semantics.

classes.label: RP
classes.definition: Polynomial-time probabilistic decision algorithms with acceptance probability ≥ 1/2 on members and 0 on nonmembers.

classes.label: coRP
classes.definition: Complements of RP languages; polynomial-time algorithms accepting members with probability 1 and nonmembers with probability ≤ 1/2.

classes.label: ZPP
classes.definition: Languages with zero-error randomized algorithms of expected polynomial running time; equivalently RP ∩ coRP.

classes.label: BPP
classes.definition: Polynomial-time probabilistic algorithms accepting members with probability ≥ 2/3 and nonmembers with probability ≤ 1/3.

classes.label: UP
classes.definition: Polynomial-time nondeterministic machines having at most one accepting computation per input.

classes.label: coUP
classes.definition: Complements of UP languages.

classes.label: NP
classes.definition: Languages having polynomial-length binary witnesses checked by a deterministic polynomial-time verifier.

classes.label: coNP
classes.definition: Complements of NP languages.

classes.label: FewP
classes.definition: Languages recognized by nondeterministic polynomial-time machines having at most polynomially many accepting computations on every input.

classes.label: SPP
classes.definition: Languages whose characteristic function belongs to GapP: a polynomial-time nondeterministic machine has accepting-minus-rejecting gap 1 on members and 0 otherwise.

classes.label: C₌P
classes.definition: Languages L for which some GapP function g satisfies x ∈ L iff g(x) = 0. GapP functions are differences of #P functions.

classes.label: PP
classes.definition: Polynomial-time probabilistic algorithms whose acceptance probability is > 1/2 exactly on members; equivalently some GapP function is positive exactly on members.

classes.label: ⊕P
classes.definition: Languages recognized when a nondeterministic polynomial-time machine has an odd number of accepting computations.

classes.label: AWPP
classes.definition: For every polynomial r, there are g in GapP and a polynomial p with 0 ≤ g(x)/2^p(|x|) ≤ 1, at least 1−2^(−r(|x|)) on members and at most 2^(−r(|x|)) on nonmembers.

classes.label: LWPP
classes.definition: There are g in GapP and an integer-valued FP function f, nonzero on unary inputs, with g(x) = f(1^|x|) for members and g(x) = 0 for nonmembers.

classes.label: WPP
classes.definition: There are g in GapP and an integer-valued FP function f, nonzero on every input, with g(x) = f(x) for members and g(x) = 0 for nonmembers.

classes.label: MA
classes.definition: Total languages with polynomial-length classical proofs followed by a probabilistic polynomial-time verifier: some proof accepts members with probability ≥ 2/3, every proof accepts nonmembers with probability ≤ 1/3.

classes.label: coMA
classes.definition: Complements of total languages in MA.

classes.label: AM
classes.definition: Total languages with a public-coin two-message protocol: Arthur sends polynomially many random bits, Merlin responds with a polynomial-length string, then a deterministic polynomial-time predicate decides; completeness ≥ 2/3, soundness ≤ 1/3.

classes.label: coAM
classes.definition: Complements of total languages in AM.

classes.label: QCMA
classes.definition: Total languages verified by polynomial-time uniform quantum circuits and polynomial-length classical witnesses, with completeness ≥ 2/3 and soundness ≤ 1/3. Fix a standard finite universal algebraic gate set.

classes.label: QMA
classes.definition: Total languages verified by polynomial-time uniform quantum circuits and polynomial-qubit quantum witnesses, with completeness ≥ 2/3 and soundness ≤ 1/3. Fix a standard finite universal algebraic gate set.

classes.label: coQMA
classes.definition: Complements of total languages in QMA.

classes.label: BQP
classes.definition: Total languages decided by polynomial-time uniform quantum circuits with error at most 1/3 on every input. Fix a standard finite universal algebraic gate set.

classes.label: SBP
classes.definition: There are f in #P and polynomial p such that f(x) ≥ 2^p(|x|) on members and f(x) ≤ 2^(p(|x|)−1) on nonmembers; #P counts accepting computations of nondeterministic polynomial-time machines.

classes.label: SZK
classes.definition: Total languages with an interactive statistical zero-knowledge proof: polynomial-time verifier, completeness ≥ 2/3 and soundness ≤ 1/3, and polynomial-time simulation of every efficient cheating verifier with negligible statistical error (auxiliary input allowed).

classes.label: NP ∩ coNP
classes.definition: Intersection of the language classes NP and coNP.

classes.label: Σ₂P
classes.definition: Languages expressible by a polynomial-time predicate with a polynomial-length existential witness followed by a polynomial-length universal witness; equivalently NP^NP.

classes.label: Π₂P
classes.definition: Complements of Σ₂P languages.

classes.label: Δ₂P
classes.definition: P^NP: deterministic polynomial time with adaptive membership queries to an NP-complete language.

classes.label: Θ₂P
classes.definition: P^NP[O(log n)]: deterministic polynomial time with O(log n) adaptive queries to an NP-complete language; equivalently polynomially many nonadaptive queries.

classes.label: PH
classes.definition: Union of Σ_kP over fixed k ≥ 0, with Σ_0P=P and Σ_(k+1)P=NP^(Σ_kP).

classes.label: P/poly
classes.definition: Languages decided by deterministic polynomial-time machines with a polynomial-length advice string for each input length, with no computability requirement on advice; equivalently arbitrary polynomial-size Boolean circuit families.

classes.label: NP/poly
classes.definition: Languages decided by nondeterministic polynomial-time machines with arbitrary polynomial-length advice depending only on input length.

classes.label: PSPACE
classes.definition: Union over k of DSPACE(n^k).

classes.label: EXP
classes.definition: Union over k of DTIME(2^(n^k)).

classes.label: NEXP
classes.definition: Union over k of NTIME(2^(n^k)).

classes.label: EXPSPACE
classes.definition: Union over k of DSPACE(2^(n^k)).

classes.label: E
classes.definition: Union over constants c of DTIME(2^(cn)).

classes.label: NE
classes.definition: Union over constants c of NTIME(2^(cn)).

complements.justification: From a 0/1 GapP gap g, use 1−g.
Replace gap g by f(0^|x|)−g; the length-dependent normalizer is unchanged.
Replace gap g by f(x)−g; the FP normalizer is unchanged.
Replace approximating gap g by f−g to exchange the near-zero and near-one intervals.
If membership means integer GapP gap g>0, then 1−2g>0 holds exactly on nonmembers.
Replace GapP gap g by g+1 to exchange odd and even parity.
Flip the output bit, exchanging bounded-error acceptance and rejection.
HVSZK is closed under complement and equals SZK; Section 1 credits Okamoto and Sahai–Vadhan for the complement theorem.
coMA is defined as the set of complements of MA languages.
coAM is defined as the set of complements of AM languages.
coQMA is defined as the set of complements of QMA languages; this is not a claim QMA=coQMA.

Run an amplified BPP SAT decider while fixing one variable at a time. A union bound makes every adaptive query correct with probability at least 2/3 on satisfiable inputs. Accept only after deterministically checking the final assignment. Unsatisfiable inputs are never accepted, so SAT and then every NP language are in RP. The source provides the historical SAT self-reduction and error-amplification ingredients; this sentence is the audit derivation.

Use the formula list from Theorem 3.1 and a deterministic parity-SAT decider. Accept if any formula has an odd number of solutions. If the input is unsatisfiable, every formula is unsatisfiable and acceptance is impossible. If satisfiable, with high probability some formula has exactly one solution. Thus SAT is in RP. This uses a total parity solver and does not assume that a solver for the total-language class UP solves the Unique-SAT promise problem.

WPP⊆CeqP and the premise identify WPP=CeqP. Complement closure gives coCeqP=WPP. Therefore UP^CeqP⊆UP^WPP⊆coCeqP=WPP. D1 adds PP and parityP. No claim P^WPP=WPP is needed. See derivation D1 in research/audit-round2-cross-counting.md.
UP⊆CeqP is baseline. The hypothesis makes CeqP=UP, explicitly one of the equivalent conditions used by the proof. The PP, PH and parityP conclusions are all stated in condition (4).

C=·CeqP⊆CeqP^CeqP is unconditional operator-to-oracle simulation. The hypothesis replaces only the oracle, giving CeqP^LWPP=CeqP by established LWPP lowness for CeqP. Hence PP⊆LWPP. P^LWPP=LWPP then transports PH and parityP from P^PP. The argument does not use the unproved LWPP^LWPP=LWPP.

Discharged by D1: PP⊆UP^CeqP. Replace the oracle by parityP, then use the unconditional relativizing UP⊆parityP and parityP^parityP=parityP. This avoids relativizing the hypothesis CeqP⊆parityP. See derivation D1 in research/audit-round2-cross-counting.md.
PH⊆UP^CeqP⊆UP^coNP⊆NP^coNP=NP^NP=Sigma2P. Complementing each query swaps coNP and NP; no NP=coNP assumption. The 2026 source is corroboration, not necessary to admission.
Delta2P=P^NP⊆P^SPP=SPP. The latter equality is unconditional closure under polynomial-time Turing reductions. No measure hypothesis needed for Delta2P; PH would need an additional argument.
Delta2P=P^NP⊆P^LWPP=LWPP. FFK explicitly states SPP^LWPP=LWPP and therefore Turing closure. Do not replace this by LWPP self-lowness.
P^AWPP⊆UP^AWPP⊆AWPP and reverse containment uses one oracle query. Replace NP only in oracle position.

Classical adaptive oracle calls can each be simulated with error at most 1/(100q(n)); a union bound across q(n) queries gives bounded error. No coherent oracle theorem is required for P^BQP⊆BQP. Total-language correctness on every query is essential.
Delta2P=P^NP⊆P^parityP=parityP. Only the oracle changes.
Theta2P=P_parallel^NP. The query list is unchanged when the same total NP oracle is regarded as a WPP language. WPP truth-table closure suffices; unrestricted Turing closure is not asserted.

First amplify the outer BP reduction to error≤1/12 using parityP closure under deterministic oracle reductions; then answer its total parity language by BPP with error≤1/12. The resulting success gap is at least 5/6 versus 1/6, hence BPP.
As in the BPP case, amplify the outer BP reduction and the BQP decision subroutine before composition. Classical randomness is available in BQP; the target parity language is total.
Both target languages lie in P^PP, replace PP by AWPP, and use P^AWPP=AWPP.
Both target languages lie in P^PP. Replace the PP oracle and use amplified classical adaptive BQP subroutine simulation.
P^PP⊆P^parityP=parityP. Remove the second submitted conclusion parityP⊆parityP: it is reflexive and contributes no consequence.
PH and parityP lie in P^PP. Replace the oracle by SPP and invoke P^SPP=SPP.
PH and parityP lie in P^PP. Replace the oracle by LWPP and invoke P^LWPP=LWPP, not LWPP^LWPP=LWPP.

Discharged by D2, which only needs the exact-count language in A0PP. CeqP⊆QMA and QMA⊆A0PP supply that. Common encoded query length makes the amplified threshold independent of the guessed count. Nonnegative gaps prevent cancellations and a polynomially large exponent defeats all wrong guesses. Apply the same argument to parityP∈P^#P[1] for the second endpoint. See derivation D2 in research/audit-round2-cross-counting.md.

audit_limitations: Historical classification review and its residual uncertainty are recorded in research/baseline-audit.json and the versioned audit dossiers. Absence from the relation closure alone does not certify that a pair was open.
No paper proof in this file is machine-checked. Lean semantics must not turn citations into hidden axioms or declare abstract graph soundness to be a mechanized proof of the cited theorems.

The benchmark-specific elementary derivations, including nonuniform witnesses, space simulations, padding and advice diagonalization, received independent mathematical cross-review in the audit dossiers. Their existing proofs are trusted rather than re-formalized.

Quantitative hardness, fine-grained improvements, promise problems, search/function classes, algebraic classes VP/VNP, and independence metatheorems need richer propositions than ordered language-class pairs.
E ⊄ Ppoly does not by itself justify BPP ⊆ P via IW1997. The required premise is an exponential circuit lower bound with appropriate quantifiers over lengths.
Kannan fixed-degree circuit lower bounds do not establish Sigma2P ⊄ Ppoly. Do not reverse quantifiers over language and polynomial degree.
Toda gives PH ⊆ P^PP, not PH ⊆ PP. A low-level PH collapse does not automatically collapse counting classes.
BPP = P for total languages does not automatically derandomize promise-BPP verifiers; do not infer MA = NP or BQP = P.
No oracle or communication-complexity separation can be imported as an unrelativized language-class separation.
Primary-source publication dates are historical bibliographic dates. Search-engine crawl dates and stale PDF template footers were not used as publication dates.

Historical review is recorded in research/baseline-audit.json and the versioned audit dossiers. Decisions about open status are evidence-based, revisable judgments; neither the relation closure nor a negative search proves absence of all pre-cutoff results.
No unrelativized strict separation between BQP and BPP, NP and BQP, or QMA and QCMA is seeded. Oracle results do not resolve those ordered pairs.

A promise-class inclusion restricts to a total-language inclusion. A separation witnessed only by a promise problem need not yield a total-language separation. The benchmark currently misses that second type of result.
BPP=P for total languages does not by itself permit replacing a verifier's promise-BPP problem by a P machine. In particular this file does not encode BPP=P implies MA=NP or QCMA=NP.
The q-gsv99 equivalence between NISZK=BPP and SZK=BPP is explicitly for promise classes and is not encoded for the total-language roster.
Neither SBP nor CeqP is assigned self-complement closure. Their complement closure is not known here; this is not a proven nonclosure.
parityP contained in PP is not a known seed. Exact parity and a threshold are different counting conditions.
Do not encode BPP=P implies NEXP not contained in Ppoly: Kabanets–Impagliazzo gives a disjunction with an arithmetic circuit lower bound, which this pair-only rule language cannot express.

The nonuniform circuit convention is essential. Nonuniform AC0 already contains undecidable length languages and must not be included in P or L. Its known reverse separations from all decidable roster classes should be provided by the classical baseline.

All source years are document/publication years, not the search engine's sometimes misleading crawl or republication date. Later revisions require a pinned historical-version audit before eligibility is frozen.

policy.cutoff_convention: Results publicly available before 2026-09-02 00:00:00 UTC count as pre-cutoff. Historical decisions check exact public versions and are revisable.
policy.point_unit: One ordered class pair certified open at cutoff and newly resolved by an accepted proof, disproof, or ZFC-independence metatheorem.
policy.baseline_meaning: Historical pre-cutoff results earn zero by definition. Zero does not assert that no post-cutoff public result exists.
policy.scenario_eligibility: Frozen questions absent from the baseline closure. The dated historical-review registry determines which are eligible for official points.
policy.independence: Separate metatheorem establishing neither ZFC proof of inclusion nor ZFC proof of its negation, unconditionally or conditional on Con(ZFC) or arithmetic soundness of ZFC. Arithmetic soundness means every first-order arithmetic sentence whose standard set-theoretic translation ZFC proves is true in the standard natural numbers. The exact premise must remain explicit in the proof, expert review and public result. No stronger unproved assumption is permitted. Independence does not enter ordinary relation closure.
policy.credit: Union of resolved eligible ordered pairs from accepted proof artifacts within one run; no duplicate credit and no pooling across runs.
policy.admission: Model runs are open. Existing cited proofs are trusted. Official run scores require run-integrity review, adjudication of all proof candidates, verification of new ordinary proofs, and a recorded historical decision for every positively scored pair. Release-wide historical decisions can satisfy that requirement.
policy.unit_of_evaluation: One exact AI model snapshot and configuration in one recorded, budgeted evaluation run.
policy.baseline_trust: Cited pre-cutoff results, implications, and operational model conventions are explicit trusted inputs. Re-formalizing existing proofs is not a launch requirement.
policy.new_proof_verification: Ordinary new claims require sandboxed Lean checking against the exact class targets with an explicit trusted-baseline axiom whitelist. Independence uses a separate expert metatheory review.
policy.ranking: Compare runs only within the same frozen taskset, declared task assignment, access track, and resource budget. Subsets are allowed and labeled.

independence_premises.unconditional: No additional consistency or soundness premise.
independence_premises.zfc_arithmetic_soundness: Every closed first-order arithmetic sentence whose standard translation is provable in ZFC is true in standard N.
